# Defaults That Use Other Variables

A variable's `default` can be built from other variables, such as `default: "{{ .ProjectName }}-state"`. Runbooks fills in the real value when it renders, using whatever the other fields hold at that moment.

The form never shows the `{{ }}` syntax. A linked default shows its text with a chip for each variable or block output it uses. A chip shows the value it links to, with a link icon, and follows that field as you edit it. Until that value is known, the chip names the variable, the way its field is labelled, or the output. A default that does more than insert a variable (a conditional or a function) appears as one chip, with the value it comes to or what it's based on. A chip is yellow while it waits on a block output that hasn't been produced.

- **Hover** over a linked value to see its expression.
- **Click** a chip to type another value in its place. The reset button next to it brings the chip back.
- **Click the X** to clear the whole value and type your own.
- **Click Reset** next to the field's name to go back to the default.

## In an Inputs block

`ServiceName` defaults to the app name with a `-service` suffix. Change `AppName` and watch the **Service Name** field and the preview below follow it.

<Inputs id="naming">
```yaml
variables:
  - name: AppName
    type: string
    description: Name of the application
    default: web
  - name: ServiceName
    type: string
    description: Defaults to the app name with a "-service" suffix
    default: "{{ .AppName }}-service"
```
</Inputs>

<TemplateInline id="naming-preview" inputsId="naming" outputPath="service.txt">
```txt
Service name: {{ .inputs.ServiceName }}
```
</TemplateInline>

## Waiting on a script's output

A default can also use another block's output, such as an ID a script prints. Until that block has run, the form can't know the value, so the chip is yellow. Hover over it to see which block it's waiting for. If no block on the page has the id the default names, the chip is red instead, and the field shows an error until you replace the value.

`AccountAlias` defaults to `acme-` plus the ID of the account that the **Create Account** script below creates. Run the script and the field shows `acme-123456789012`. Or click the chip and type an ID yourself.

<Inputs id="account">
```yaml
variables:
  - name: AccountAlias
    type: string
    description: Defaults to "acme-" plus the ID of the account the script below creates
    default: "acme-{{ .outputs.create_account.account_id }}"
```
</Inputs>

A block's `id` uses `-`, but a template refers to it with `_`, so `create-account` is `.outputs.create_account`.

<Command
  id="create-account"
  path="scripts/create-account.sh"
  title="Create Account"
  description="Simulates creating an account and outputs its ID as account_id"
/>

## In a Template

This template's `boilerplate.yml` has linked defaults of every kind:

- `BucketName` is the project name plus `-state`.
- `ReplicaBucket` is the same as `BucketName`.
- `InstanceSize` depends on `Environment`.
- `CatalogRepositories` has an entry built from the project name.
- `DefaultTags` has a key and a value built from other variables.

Generate it, then change `ProjectName` or `Environment` and look at `settings.yml`.

<Template id="linked-defaults" path="templates/linked-defaults" />
